title: Unconditional |bracelets(4,2)| = 6 via a Concrete Dihedral Action
description: Answers the first open question of burnside-counting-oq-04: build a concrete dihedral action on the binary colourings of the 4-cycle and recover the bracelet count without taking the necklace count or reflection total as hypotheses, and without native_decide. We define the faithful permutation representation ρ : DihedralGroup 4 →* Equiv.Perm (ZMod 4) sending r i to (x ↦ x + i) and sr i to (x ↦ -i - x) — the reflection form -i-x (not i-x) is exactly what makes ρ a homomorphism for Mathlib's dihedral multiplication convention sr i * sr j = r (j - i) — and lift it to colourings Coloring = ZMod 4 → Fin 2 by (g • c) p = c ((ρ g)⁻¹ p), a genuine MulAction because ρ is a hom. Burnside's lemma (MulAction.sum_card_fixedBy_eq_card_orbits_mul_card_group) gives Σ_{g ∈ D₄} |Fix(g)| = |Coloring / D₄| · |D₄|. The fixed-point sum evaluates to 48 by KERNEL decide (8 group elements × 16 colourings: 16+2+4+2 for rotations, 8+8+4+4 for reflections), and |D₄| = 8 (DihedralGroup.card), so |bracelets| · 8 = 48, i.e. |bracelets| = 6 — unconditionally. The parent's binary_four_bracelet_count assumed both the necklace count (6) and the reflection total (24); both are now subsumed by the single kernel-decided sum. #print axioms confirms only propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound — no Lean.ofReduceBool (no native_decide) and no sorryAx.

overview.historicalContext: Burnside's lemma counts the orbits of a finite group action as the average number of fixed points. For the cyclic rotation group ℤ/nℤ on the beads of an n-cycle it yields the necklace numbers; for the larger dihedral group D_n, which adjoins the n reflections, it yields the bracelet numbers (OEIS A000029). The parent entry burnside-counting computes the length-4 binary necklace count (6) but closes the orbit enumeration with native_decide; its dihedral extension oq-04 proves the abstract index-2 folding identity and recovers the bracelet count only conditionally, assuming the necklace count and reflection total as hypotheses because it never builds a concrete dihedral action. Realising that action and discharging the counts by an axiom-free kernel computation is the natural completion.
overview.problemStatement: Build a concrete dihedral action on the binary colourings of the 4-cycle and prove |bracelets(4,2)| = 6 unconditionally — without assuming the necklace count or reflection total, and without native_decide (kernel decide only).
overview.text: With ρ : DihedralGroup 4 →* Equiv.Perm (ZMod 4) the faithful representation r i ↦ (·+i), sr i ↦ (-i-·), and the colouring action (g • c) p = c ((ρ g)⁻¹ p), Burnside gives Σ_{g ∈ D₄} |Fix(g)| = |bracelets|·8. Kernel decide evaluates the sum to 48, so |bracelets| = 6.
overview.proofStrategy: First fix the permutation representation ρ: rotations r i act on positions by x ↦ x + i and reflections sr i by x ↦ -i - x; the reflection form -i-x (rather than i-x) is dictated by Mathlib's convention sr i * sr j = r (j - i), and posPerm_mul checks the homomorphism property in all four (r/sr)×(r/sr) cases by ext + ZMod arithmetic. Lift to colourings via (g • c) p = c ((ρ g)⁻¹ p); one_smul and mul_smul follow from ρ.map_one and ρ.map_mul. Register DecidablePred and Fintype instances for the fixed-point sets and a decidable orbit relation for the quotient Fintype. Apply Burnside's lemma to get Σ |Fix(g)| = |X/G|·|G|; evaluate the left side to 48 by kernel decide (8 symmetries, 16 colourings) and rewrite |D₄| = 8 via DihedralGroup.card; omega finishes 48 = |bracelets|·8 ⇒ |bracelets| = 6. The orbit quotient is never enumerated by decide — only the cheap fixed-point sum is — which is what keeps the computation within kernel reach.
keyInsights: The reflection must act as x ↦ -i - x, not the geometrically tempting x ↦ i - x: only the former makes the position assignment a homomorphism for Mathlib's dihedral multiplication convention sr i * sr j = r (j - i)

Burnside lets one avoid enumerating the orbit quotient (the expensive step the parent did with native_decide): only the fixed-point sum needs evaluation, and that is light enough for kernel decide (8 × 16 checks over Fin-based data)

The single fixed-point sum 48 subsumes both hypotheses the parent assumed — the necklace contribution (16+2+4+2 = 24 from the rotations) and the reflection total (8+8+4+4 = 24 from the reflections) — so the count becomes unconditional
Representing positions as ZMod 4 and colours as Fin 2 keeps every object Fin-based, so kernel reduction of the action and the decidable-equality of colourings stays cheap
prerequisites: Group actions, orbits, and the orbit-counting (Burnside/Cauchy–Frobenius) lemma
The dihedral group DihedralGroup n and its multiplication table
Decidable equality and Fintype enumeration for kernel decide

sections.title: Unconditional Bracelet Count via Burnside
sections.summary: Kernel decide gives Σ_{g ∈ D₄} |Fix(g)| = 48; Burnside's lemma and |D₄| = 8 force |bracelets| · 8 = 48, hence |bracelets| = 6 — with no necklace or reflection hypotheses.

crossReferences.description: Discharges the first open question of oq-04: builds the concrete dihedral action oq-04 leaves unbuilt and removes the necklace-count and reflection-total hypotheses of its binary_four_bracelet_count, yielding the unconditional |bracelets| = 6.
Upgrades the parent's length-4 binary necklace count (closed with native_decide) to the dihedral bracelet count, discharged by kernel decide and so axiom-free.

conclusion.summary: Building the concrete dihedral action ρ : DihedralGroup 4 →* Equiv.Perm (ZMod 4) and lifting it to binary colourings turns the conditional bracelet count of oq-04 into an unconditional, axiom-free one: Burnside's lemma plus a single kernel-decided fixed-point sum (Σ |Fix(g)| = 48) and |D₄| = 8 give |bracelets(4,2)| = 6 with no native_decide and no assumed counts.
conclusion.implications: Demonstrates that the bracelet count is reachable by kernel computation when the action is kept Fin-based and only the cheap fixed-point sum (not the orbit quotient) is evaluated — a template for axiom-free dihedral orbit counts that the parent oq-04 could only state conditionally.
openQuestions: Generalise the concrete action and kernel-decided fixed-point sum to D_n for small n (e.g. n = 5, 6), recovering b(5) = 8 and b(6) = 13 unconditionally, and chart where kernel decide stops being feasible.

Combine this concrete action with the rotation counts k^gcd(n,r) (oq-03) and reflection counts k^((n+1)/2) (oq-05) to prove a closed form for the binary bracelet numbers b(n) without per-n computation.
